Item: How will plumbing pass through the cabinet?
Prompt / specification: A large improvised cutout can destroy drawer space, back stiffness, and service access. Options: Map a bounded service chase from real fixture locations | Use a removable false back around a known service zone | Cut the cabinet after the plumber arrives

The sink bowl, drain, supplies, and countertop clips occupy a three-dimensional envelope. Options: Model each drawer against the measured fixture envelope | Use one shallow top drawer and doors below | Order full-depth drawers before selecting the sink

Item: How should exposed panel edges be protected?
Prompt / specification: Bathroom splashes and cleaning water concentrate at toe kicks, sink edges, and floor-adjacent seams. Options: Seal every machined edge with a compatible documented system | Use factory-finished panels and matching edge banding | Rely on countertop caulk to protect the cabinet

Prompt / specification: Drawer travel or diagonals change as the vanity is pulled against wall or floor variation.
Project value / evidence: Release attachment, level with shims at structural bearing points, restore square, and refasten without distortion.

Prompt / specification: The vanity fits the actual room and fixture stack while keeping storage smooth, wet edges protected, and every shutoff and trap serviceable.
The cabinet is level and square after anchoring, with the top supported at every designed bearing location.
Doors and drawers complete full travel without entering the sink, faucet, drain, supply, clip, or wall envelope.
